method.label: Count color rows in three blocks

annotationRationale: The derivation uses equally likely color rows and permutations with repeated colors. Combinations select the permitted positions, and the multiplication principle combines the choices.
sourceMethod: Followed the official row-arrangement method, with consecutive blocks representing players. Clarified equal likelihood and why the recipient assignments do not overlap.

review.mathCheck: There are \(12!/(3!2!1!6!)=55{,}440\) equally likely color rows. The six distinct recipient assignments each allow \(\binom43\binom42\binom41=96\) successful rows, giving 576 successes. Thus the probability is \(4/385\), and \(m+n=389\), choice C, matching the key.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Q16 on page 9. It retains the official color-row and four-position-block count while explicitly explaining equal likelihood and the absence of duplicate recipient assignments.
review.annotationCheck: The sample space, positional restrictions, disjoint recipient assignments and fraction reduction are all justified. The explanation is self-contained at AMC 12 level.
